fullPassage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status — they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.

questions.passage: When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By __________ (produce) goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 전치사 By 뒤에는 동명사가 오므로 produce → producing으로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: 'By ___ goods'에서 전치사 by의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사(-ing)가 필요하다. produce → producing

questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status — they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely __________ to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: locked in(묶인/고착된). 소비자가 그 제품에 완전히 '묶여' 있지 않을 수 있으므로 완벽한 보완재라 단정하지 말라는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
① paid off(다 갚은): 문맥 부적합

② turned away(돌려보내진): 문맥 부적합

③ locked in(묶인) ←정답: 'customers may not be completely ___ to the product'에 어울림 — 특정 제품에 매여 있음

④ given up(포기된): 문맥 부적합

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: consumed together(함께 소비되는). 완벽한 보완재는 램프와 전구처럼 반드시 '함께 소비되어야' 한다.
det.analysis:
① sold separately(따로 판매되는): 완벽한 보완재 개념과 반대

② consumed together(함께 소비되는) ←정답: 'such as a lamp and a lightbulb'라는 예시가 함께 써야 하는 관계를 보여줌

③ produced locally(현지에서 생산되는): 문맥 부적합

④ priced equally(같은 값이 매겨지는): 문맥 부적합
